rule: Unary minus binds tighter than exponentiation: -2^2 evaluates as (-2)^2, not -(2^2).
FileMaker suppresses the leading zero on a fractional number with no integer part: 0.25 displays as .25.
GetAsBoolean treats an error result as true.
Numeric truthiness (If, Case, GetAsBoolean) follows the same leading-digit extraction rule as GetAsNumber: text with a leading digit is truthy, text without one is falsy.
GetAsNumber strips non-numeric characters and concatenates the remaining digits, rather than truncating at the first non-numeric character.
Text comparison (=) is case-insensitive by default. <> and ≠ are equivalent ASCII/symbol spellings of not-equal.
Let() evaluates bindings left to right, allows a later binding to shadow an earlier one in the same Let, and a nested Let reverts its outer scope on exit.
Case() with no default result returns empty string, not an error, and stops at the first true test even when a later test is also true.
String indexing is 1-based; position 0 behaves the same as position 1; requesting more characters than exist returns the whole string rather than erroring.
Substitute is case-sensitive; Position and PatternCount are not - an inconsistency between functions that otherwise seem like a family.
Trim strips only spaces, not tabs or other whitespace.
Block comments (/* */) nest correctly.
ValueCount and related list functions recognize CR and LF as equivalent separators, with or without a trailing separator.
A timestamp's serial number decomposes exactly as (date serial - 1) x 86400 + time serial. Date(1;1;1)'s own serial number is 1; Time()'s serial number is total seconds since midnight.

EvaluationError codes verified against error-codes.md: 1207 unbalanced parenthesis, 1202 too many parameters, 1204 zero arguments given where at least one is required (not 1201, which is for some-but-not-enough), 1205 unterminated comment, 1206 unterminated string, 1212 operator expected between adjacent literals (not the more general 1208), 102 missing field, 15 divide by zero. EvaluationError must wrap the Evaluate() call itself, not a variable already holding its result, or it returns 0 regardless of the real error.

Standard arithmetic precedence holds (*/^ tighter than +, & looser than +, comparison looser than AND, AND tighter than OR); // and /* */ comments strip correctly at any position, including containing quote characters, and comment markers inside an actual string literal are treated as literal text.
NOT binds tighter than ^: NOT 2^0 evaluates as (NOT 2)^0, not NOT(2^0).
^ is left-associative, not right-associative: 2^3^2 evaluates as (2^3)^2 = 64, not 2^(3^2) = 512 - the opposite of the convention most general-purpose languages use.
Comparison chains and OR/XOR are ordinary same-tier left-to-right evaluation, not special-cased: 1<2<3 evaluates as (1<2)<3; 1 OR 0 XOR 1 evaluates as (1 OR 0) XOR 1.

A leading + sign is accepted as a no-op; scientific notation (1e3) is accepted and computed correctly; a 30-digit integer literal loses no precision; a literal with more than one decimal point, a trailing decimal point with no digits after it, and digit-group underscores are all rejected outright.

GetAsDate/GetAsTime/GetAsTimestamp outside their documented valid range (year 1-4000) return an error rather than clamping. GetAsTime passes an out-of-range hour through unchanged as text. GetAsTime correctly applies the am/pm designator when present (corrected from an earlier, wrong claim that it was discarded, based on not checking the am case directly).

U+2028 and U+2029 work as ValueCount separators, same as CR/LF; a bare Char()/Code() round-trip preserves the character correctly; adjacent CR and LF count as two separate separators, not one combined one.
Date/Time/Timestamp arithmetic rolls over correctly for overflow (month 13, day 0, day 35, hour/minute overflow) and handles leap years correctly (2000 is a leap year, 2001 is not).
WordCount treats = as a word boundary and does not create empty words from consecutive spaces. Filter is case-sensitive and returns empty for an empty filter text.
A field name containing a space is referenced directly in a calc with no special quoting.
Bracket syntax accesses a specific repetition of a repeating field; List() over a repeating field returns a CR-delimited list of its repetition values in order.

Round always rounds up at 0.5 (round-half-up, not round-half-to-even); a negative half rounds away from zero, not toward positive infinity (Round(-14.5;0) -> -15); a negative precision argument rounds to tens/hundreds/thousands.

Log(0) and Lg(0) both error (return ?), despite their own docs saying 0 'returns nothing' - that phrase means "produces no valid result" (an error), not literally an empty string. Ln(0) also errors, consistent with its own docs which explicitly name 0 as an error case (unlike Log/Lg's more ambiguous wording).

Tan(Radians(90)) does not error despite the docs stating 90 degrees 'cannot be used' - it returns a specific, very large floating-point number, consistent with Radians(90) not landing exactly on the mathematical asymptote in double precision.
